absent: Submission ordering and completion affinity across hardware and software queues.
Budget exhaustion handling and deadlock avoidance beyond hook presence.
Timeout recovery actions and poll completion contracts.
Freeze depth counting and quiesce guarantees.
Power-management runtime behaviour beyond the empty helper.
Scatter-gather mapping failure modes and segment limits.
Plug merging and elevator interaction details.

findings.text: Multiqueue driver interface is a table of optional callbacks for submitting single and batched commands, forcing hardware kick on early stop, reserving and releasing budget with per-command token save and restore, reacting to timeouts, polling and marking completion, initializing and tearing down hardware contexts and per-command private areas, cleaning unfinished commands, reporting busyness, overriding queue mapping, and showing a command for debugging when enabled.

Tag pool bookkeeping keeps total and reserved capacities, a count of active queues, separate allocation bitmaps for normal and reserved tags, live and static command pointer tables, a list of backing pages, a spinlock guarding reference clearing before pool release, and a deferred-release callback head.

Block device object records start offset and length in sectors, links to disk and queue, per-CPU statistics, a timestamp, combined atomic state for partition number and policy flags, device number, page-cache mapping, opener count, a size-update spinlock, claiming and holder pointers with holder operations guarded by a mutex and count plus holder directory, freeze accounting with mutex, metadata pointer, writer count, optional security pointer, and an embedded generic device with randomized field layout.

Active plug state accumulates multiqueue and cached command lists, a timestamp, I/O and command counts, flags for spanning queues and elevator presence, and a callback list; a command list is a head and tail pair; a callback entry chains a list node with a function pointer receiving a schedule-origin flag plus opaque data.

User mapping descriptor holds a page pointer array, offset, page order, entry count, and two booleans for null mapping and user origin; request iteration state pairs a segment iterator with the current bio.

Queue behaviour modifiers use distinct low bits for shared tag queues, stacking on lower multiqueue devices, shared hardware-context tags, blocking allocation, round-robin tag choice, and opt-out of default scheduling on single or shared queues, with a sentinel marking the limit.

Depth ceiling is ten thousand two hundred forty; absent hardware-context index is maximum unsigned; hardware-context visibility uses four ordered values for stopped, tag active, scheduler restart and CPU-offline inactive plus a count; unique tag reserves sixteen low bits for tag and carries hardware-context index above them.
Allocation behaviour uses three separate low bits for immediate failure when empty, reserved-pool use, and power-management marking.
Sector shift is nine with size five hundred twelve bytes; sectors per page derive from page shift minus sector shift; sector mask is one less than that count.

Completion outcome is an eight-bit bitwise value with sixteen-bit short alias; success is zero and distinct small integers identify unsupported, timeout, space, transport, target, reservation conflict, medium, protection, resource, I/O error, device-mapper requeue, retry, device resource, zone open resource, zone active resource, offline, duration limit and invalid, with eighteen skipped.

Partition number occupies low eight bits capped at two hundred fifty-five with higher bits for read-only policy, writer holder, submit capability, read-only warning and optional fail injection; absent queue cookie is maximum unsigned; operation flags are thirty-two-bit bitwise and queue cookie is plain unsigned; three headers define single include guards.

Hardware-context visibility progresses among stopped, tag-active, scheduler-restart and inactive, where inactive means all associated CPUs went offline; names stay synchronized with the numeric order.

Command state distinguishes idle from started and completed; started means any non-idle value and completed means the terminal value; transitions to completed use single stores, with a direct variant that stores then invokes a caller-supplied completion routine.

Command lookup by tag fails closed with null when the index reaches total capacity, otherwise hints the entry for fetch and returns it; unique-tag decoding extracts hardware-context index by right shift and tag by low-bit mask.

Completion batching rejects missing containers, scheduler-tagged commands, and for non-passthrough commands any end callback or error; the first accepted completion callback sticks and later mismatches are rejected while timestamp need is accumulated and the command joins the tail; timestamp need reflects statistics or scheduler flags and reservation reflects a dedicated flag.

Position and lengths come from stored sector, data length and statistics fields with sector conversion by shift; data presence excludes discard-like operations; current length uses first bio size for dataless cases else first vector length; payload length and vector prefer special payload when flagged; physical segment count collapses to one for special payload while discard count floors at one; bio and vector totals count chain members.

Bio iteration guards empty chains and walks linked bios; segment and vector iteration nests bio walk with per-bio segment walk; last-element test requires no next bio and iterator at end; hardware-context iteration walks queue contexts by index with lookup per step and per-context iteration walks attached software contexts.

Passthrough statistics require queue opt-in via limits flag, a present bio with attached device, and payload size aligned to the device logical block size, which resolves from device to queue to limits.

Synchronous classification covers reads and any sync, flush or preflush modifier; path-error classification treats unsupported, space, target, reservation, medium and protection as non-path and every other outcome as a possible path failure suitable for retry.

Flush forwards only when a plug exists; timestamp invalidation clears cached time and flag when block-timestamp state is set; disabled-plug and power-management init operations are empty; prefetch hints a single address to the compiler builtin; whole-device, container and kobject conversions derive from disk part zero, embedded device offset and embedded kobject.

Tag reference clearing serializes under the pool spinlock; device size updates use a dedicated spinlock while holder and freeze changes use separate mutexes; hardware-context fetch runs inside a read-side critical section with ordered acquire and release around dereference.

Disk allocation supplies a private static lock class to the underlying allocator; freeze saves allocation flags around a no-save freeze and unfreeze restores them; per-command cleanup invokes driver cleanup only when installed; scatter mapping delegates with empty last-entry seed; fake-timeout check requires build option and queue flag before delegating.

Public block interface exposes the driver operation table, tag pool, device, plug and mapping descriptors, bio completion callback signature, operation-flags and queue-cookie types, plug callback signature, and small helpers for tag conversion, state query, size and position query, hardware-context fetch and statistics gating.

Driver private area is addressed immediately after the command object with reverse conversion by subtracting the command size, so size mismatch corrupts; tag fetch prefetches before return; hardware-context array access trusts caller-provided index range; empty init and no-plug operations must not be assumed to have effects.
